points.description: Step 1 – mRNA exit and travel: mRNA leaves the nucleus through a nuclear pore and travels through the cytoplasm to a ribosome (or enters the rough ER). Must be listed and described.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only one of the two ideas (exit via nuclear pore; travel to ribosome/rough ER) is given.

points.description: Step 2 – Initiation: ribosome reads the mRNA bases in triplets (codons); translation begins at a START codon in the P site.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only codons/reading in triplets or only the START codon is mentioned.

points.description: Step 3 – Codon–anticodon matching: tRNA carrying an amino acid with a complementary anticodon recognizes and pairs with the mRNA codon (A pairs with U, C with G).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if tRNA brings amino acids but complementary codon–anticodon pairing is not stated.

points.description: Step 4 – Elongation and termination: amino acids on adjacent tRNAs are bonded together (peptide bonds) and new tRNA/amino acids are added to lengthen the chain, continuing until a STOP codon is read (A site), ending the protein.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only chain elongation or only the STOP codon is given.

rubric.notes: Four steps worth 0.75 each: mRNA exit/travel, initiation/codon reading, tRNA anticodon pairing, elongation/termination. Equivalent wording is accepted. Steps must be both named/listed and described; a bare list earns about half of each point.
